title: Chalkboard: runbook actions + followups (oncall) - Zain
content:
Chalkboard-style oncall notes (quick, messy). Goal: capture follow-ups and runbook edits before I forget.

-- TL;DR --
- Pager at 02:14 UTC: spike in inference latency for hosted-us-west-2 API (approx 20m). Auto-fallback kicked in, degraded to smaller model, traffic served but elevated 95p latency.
- Root cause provisional: KV cache eviction storm after nightly GC + a bad batching config rollout (see rollout v0.9.3).
- Customer impact: small % of requests had 2x latency; no data loss; no auth failures.

02:10-02:35 UTC (timeline)
- 02:10: alert: route hosted-us-west-2 latency > 300ms p95 across route 'generation/text'
- 02:12: I jumped in, ran quick dashboard -> spike aligns with increased queue length on pods (runtime pool a-reserve-3)
- 02:14: paging team, posted summary to #sre-oncall and #prod-incidents
- 02:18: triggered canary fallback (manual) to model m-latency-2-small; traffic shifted, success rate normalizing
- 02:25: Verified autoscaler showing new instances spinning up; KV mem pressure high (OOM events on background cache process)
- 02:35: Incident declared mitigated; kept monitoring until 02:50

Commands run (copyable)
- kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=runtime -o wide --selector=pool=a-reserve-3
- kubectl -n inference logs <pod> --since=10m | grep -i "kvcache"
- curl -s "https://internal-metrics/api/route/hosted-us-west-2?window=15m" | jq '.p95'

Observations / quick hypotheses
- Nightly GC (job gc-cache-2026-03-24-23) had higher-than-usual churn; eviction callback triggered cascades in the runtime's in-process cache layer. That increased cache-miss rates and caused more synchronous KV loads back to disk/network, which increased tail latency.
- Rollout v0.9.3 changed default batching threshold from 12->8 tokens for generation routes; lower batching increased per-request overhead under high concurrency. Combined with KV pressure = worse tail.
- Metric gaps: we don't currently emit per-pod KV-eviction-rate at 1m granularity (only 5m). Need finer granularity for future root-cause.

Follow-ups (action items)
- [ACTION] Runbook edit: add checklist for "KV cache eviction storm" with immediate mitigation steps (fallback to model variant + scale pool + pause GC). Owner: Zain. Due: 2026-03-28. Linked: CONFLUENCE INF-985.
- [ACTION] Create alert for per-pod kv_eviction_rate (1m) and add to hosted-us-west-2 route dashboard. Owner: Priya Rao. Due: 2026-03-27. JIRA: JIRA-INF-2140.
- [ACTION] Revert batching threshold for generation routes to 12 tokens on canary until we profile more. Owner: Eng-runtime (Maya). Due: 2026-03-26. PR ref: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/442 (notes in PR).
- [ACTION] Postmortem? Short blameless writeup to be submitted if follow-ups > 3 items. Owner: Zain. Due: 2026-03-31.
- [ACTION] Add a step in deploy checklist to run a synthetic tail-latency canary when changing batching defaults. Owner: Release Eng. Due: 2026-04-02.

Runbook TODOs (things to add inline)
- Immediate mitigation section: exact kubectl commands + grafana links + slack templates for notifying affected teams/customers.
- Escalation matrix: include on-call SRE for dedicated pools and the model-ops contact.
- Troubleshooting flow: metrics to check in order (queue length -> p95 -> kv_eviction -> pod mem -> GC logs) with thresholds.
- Post-incident checklist: ensure rollback/forward rollout notes, include PR numbers and owners.

Questions / open items
- Is there a way to temporarily throttle GC (gc-cache job) without a full deploy? Quick patch idea: expose a GC pause via configmap and document. (If yes, add to runbook).
- Confirm whether auto-fallback keeps token accounting consistent (cost implications) — ping billing/ops.

Notes for handoff (to morning oncall)
- Watch per-pod kv_eviction_rate and queue_length on a-reserve-3 pool for next 24h.
- If see >2x baseline, trigger fallback earlier (rule: p95 > 200ms for >3m).
- Contact list: @maya (eng-runtime), @priya (sre), @lia-k (model-ops).

Misc scribbles (ideas for longer-term)
- Consider bounded async load of KV misses to avoid sync stalls (engineering spike).
- Add dynamic batching policy that adapts to observed queue depth and KV hit-rate.

References / links used during triage
- Grafana route dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/hosted-us-west-2-route
- Confluence runbook stub: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/INF-985-runbook-cache-eviction
- PR for batching change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/442
- JIRA ticket for alerting: JIRA-INF-2140

Last quick status: left notes in #sre-oncall, updated the incident channel with mitigation steps and screenshot of p95 graph. Will follow up with runbook edits tomorrow morning and ship alerts this week.

End of chalkboard dump.
